scope: Read-only inventory of the exact published/master equipment snapshot and its actually rendered weapon-vs-armor AC adjustment fields. It separates missile tables from PHB/UA hand-held melee adjustments and checks explicit AC-column alignment against the independently transcribed PHB38/UA28 source-cell receipt. This artifact does not change, grade, or approve active data or citations.

renderedDataSemantics.fieldValueRendering: At dist/app.js lines 80-99, fieldEntries enumerates item.fields; attributeRows preserves each label/value and attaches item.fieldSources[label]; compact facts and Table layout render the value. fieldValue joins array values, stringifies other values. Existing AC arrays are stored as scalar strings and render verbatim.
renderedDataSemantics.sourceNavigation: In Table layout, each equipment row includes the field source chip via the matched fieldSources entry; compact layout provides Field sources chips for cited rows.
renderedDataSemantics.search: At dist/search.js lines 34-36 and 86-96, searchableFieldsText indexes each authored field label and value into the item body. Citation/source metadata remains excluded. Thus the current array labels and values appear in the equipment search index, while the values themselves remain per-item fields.

findings.ua28ArrayValues: All existing UA p.28 per-item missile AC adjustment arrays align to the explicit AC 0–10 column order and match every corresponding cell in the pinned source truth after normalizing a minus glyph spelling. Exact field source objects and compiled bindings identify UA p.28; no numeric source mismatch was found.
findings.rawGlyphVariations: All raw-token differences are glyph-only minus variants in the two staff sling arrays: the published source transcription uses U+2212 in 11 negative cells while the independent review receipt uses ASCII hyphen. Numeric values match; original current strings remain preserved verbatim.
findings.ua28Coverage: The 24-row UA table has 21 existing per-item AC arrays across 20 owner items. The three rows with no individual AC adjustment field in the current equipment record are Hammer (owner phb-hammer), Harpoon (ua-harpoon), and Javelin (phb-javelin). These are coverage absences, not numeric mismatches; the new table projection is the appropriate place to represent the complete source table.
findings.phb38Authority: No equipment item currently has a dedicated PHB p.38 missile AC adjustment field. For 13 of 15 PHB rows, a same-row UA p.28 per-item field exists and its AC 2–10 slice matches the PHB source truth; those values remain UA-sourced fields, not PHB citations. PHB p.38 Hammer and Javelin rows have no per-item missile array.
findings.commonRows: The pinned source-cell truth confirms that all 15 shared PHB/UA table rows have identical PHB AC 2–10 and UA AC 2–10 cells. Its UA-only rows and AC0/1 columns remain UA-specific.
findings.meleeExclusion: Hand-held AC adjustment arrays citing PHB p.38 are a separate melee table family, and UA p.27 arrays are likewise hand-held melee. They were inventoried and explicitly excluded from the PHB38/UA28 missile-table denominator; their 9-cell versus 11-cell lengths do not indicate missing missile AC columns.
findings.reviewLimits: This is an array/source-authority census, not approval of any row focus, crop, context, default page group, source-value grade, table projection, mechanics, or overall equipment completeness. It relies on the exact root independent source-cell receipt and does not independently re-transcribe source pixels.
